power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: The limitations are several. Development-cohort figures are developmentset estimates: every design choice was made with sight of these data, and with 45 evaluable seizures a difference of three seizures is within sampling error [52]; four feature sets at two warning windows went through the same nested procedure and the frozen scheme tied for the highest sensitivity, so the development estimate was the best of eight. The pre-specified tests treat seizures as independent although they are nested in children; a design effect of about 1.3 would move the boundary development p-value from 0.034 to about 0.05, and the post hoc child-level analysis gives the same verdict as the pre-specified tests in every cohort while showing how unevenly the development effect was distributed. The cohorts are small for a prediction study, 65 recordings and 3565 h in all, drawn from one tertiary paediatric unit apart from CHB-MIT, with focal epilepsies mostly under presurgical evaluation and medication withdrawal, and no sociodemographic subgroup was examined. The validation had a power of 0.86 for the development effect and 0.39 for half of it, so a half-sized true effect could have been missed, although the observed validation sensitivity lies below chance rather than between chance and the development estimate. The scheme uses no spatial information, so the relation between electrode position and the epileptogenic zone, which is the natural next question for a scalp method, is untested here beyond the post hoc comparison by reported onset side. The pre-specifications are internal documents, written on the day of the freeze and deposited with a time-stamp before unblinding rather than publicly registered, and the primary rule of v2 was amended before its confirmation (13 October 2026) to add the ±1 h jitter test. The Siegmund approximation used to prune the CUSUM grid omits the overshoot correction; corrected, the nominal false-alarm rate of the frozen thresholds is about 0.02 per hour, more than twenty times below the rates realised, a gap explained by the autocorrelation of interictal z (lag-1 about 0.5) and by non-zero per-child interictal means (-0.62 to +0.16). Calibration needs 8 h and therefore excludes short recordings and the first night; quality control discards one window in five; the zero-phase filter is offline; and the alarm-eligible denominator makes the false-alarm rate higher than the number of alarms per hour of recording. The sleep-wake gold standard is the clinicians' routine review marks, which cover 7727 windows (about 21 h, 1.6% of all windows), not polysomnographic staging. One recording delivered in both batches was recognised as a duplicate only after unblinding and entered no performance figure; validation data should be de-duplicated by file identity before the run. The comparators were re-implemented from their descriptions; not reproducing their published performance under our rules says nothing about the original studies beyond their lack of a chance comparison.

Development-cohort estimates and power. Development-cohort estimates are nested leave-one-patient-out: each held-out child's weights and CUSUM parameters, including the parameter search, come from the other 19 children only, whereas the vigilance estimator, the quality-control thresholds and the choice among candidate feature sets were fixed with sight of the whole cohort. Horizon, ring, percentile-profile and clock-matched analyses use interictal blocks more than 8 h from any seizure and are exploratory; other tests are named where they are reported, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for per-child segment tests (Supplementary Table S3). The sensitivity-time-inwarning curve thresholds the 5-min causal moving average of z and holds the warning for 30 min; per-patient results and the alarm-level positive predictive value are descriptive. The power of the analytic test at the development effect and at half of it (Supplementary Note S1) was 0.55 and 0.20 for the 51 seizures counted in batch 2, 0.63 and 0.26 for the 50 counted in CHB-MIT and 0.86 and 0.39 for the 101 pooled, all counted before the locked run. The pooled analysis of both validation cohorts is primary, each cohort is also reported, and no cohort may be dropped after results are seen. Analyses used Python 3.14 with NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn.

stat_p_nonsig.report:
Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is 'no effect', 'no difference', or that groups are 'the same' after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is 'not significantly' different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.
